BACONC PILIP'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.qov.ph OPINION NO. Ll_ MR. NARCISO PELINIO Brgy. Batobato, San Isidro Davao Oriental narcisopelinio@gmail.com Dear Mr. Pelinio: This has reference to your inquiry through email requesting for guidance on the following matters, we quote in verbatim, to wit: (I) Allowed ba si Atty. Mark Joseph M. Virgilio (Atty. Mark) na isang Contract Of Service na mag represent on behalf of the LGU-SIDO sa lahat ng mga events or activities? We all know that there's no employer-employee relationship between LGU-SIDO at sa kanya; (2) Based on their reply sa kanyang status sa contract of service with regards on his duties and functions, is it okay lang po ba ang kanyang status sa COA guidelines ? (3) Again, based on their reply po sa akin lalo na sa hinihingi ko na payroll for the Month of January 2024 and February 2024 ni Atty. Mark. Is it necessary po ba na secure ako ng Special Power of Attorney (SPA) despite na ako na personal po ang humingi sa kanila? It was stated in my email (sic) request with regard (sic) to my purpose/intention and as far as I know it is a public document. We note the reply of the Human Resource Management Division which provided Atty. Mark's duties and responsibilities as the Mayor's Chief of Staff and Legal Officer. We shall answer the first and second issues together as both are interrelated. We cite the CSC Memorandum Circular No. 38, Series of 1993, which categorically made the distinction between contract of services/job orders and contractual and plantilla appointment, declaring that services rendered under contracts of services and job orders are non-government services which do not have to be submitted to the CSC for approval. For purposes of determining the existence of employer-employee relationship, the Court has consistently adhered to the four-fold test, namely: (I) whether the alleged employer has the power of selection and engagement of an employee; (2) whether he has control of the employee with respect to the means and methods by which work is to be accomplished; (3) whether he has the power to dismiss; and (4) whether the employee was paid wages. Of the four, the control test is the most important elementl. 1 Lopez etal vs. Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System, G.R. No. 154472, JurE 30, 2005. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

We agree that there is no employer-employee relationship by virtue of the engagement of Atty. Mark through a contract of service. On the other hand, it is important to discuss that while Atty. Mark is merely holding a contractual obligation, his position is one that requires a high degree of trust and confidence of his appointing authority. The Supreme Court elucidated on the matter, to wit: We stress that a primarily confidential position is characterized by the close proximity of the positions of the appointer and appointee as well as the high degree of trust and confidence inherent in their relationship. Among those positions judicially determined as primarily confidential positions are the following: Chief Legal Counsel of the Philippine National Bank; Confidential Agent of the Office of the Auditor, GSIS; Secretary of the Sangguniang Bayan; Secretary to the City Mayor; Senior Security and Security Guard in the Office of the Vice Mayor; Secretary to the Board of a government corporation; City Legal Counsel, City Legal Officer or City Attorney (emphasis supplied); Provincial Attomey; Private Secretary; and Board Secretary II of the Philippine State College of Aeronautics. The Court in these instances focused on the nature of the functions of the office characterized by such "close intimacy' between the appointee and appointing power which insures freedom of intercourse without embarrassment or freedom from misgivings of betrayals of personal trust or confidential matters of state2. Here, Atty. Mark, acting as the Mayor's Chief of Staff and the Citys Legal Officer, holds a confidential position. Atty. Mark can validly represent the local government unit (LGU) as he binds himself to render service or in representation of his appointing authority, with the consent or authority of the latter. As long as the City Mayor holds Atty. Mark in his representation, Atty. Mark may validly perform the duties and functions of his office. In addition, it is the Civil Service Commission (CSC) and not the Commission on Audit (COA) which is mandated by the 1987 Constitution to regulate the employment and working conditions of civil servants. Moreso, the CSC in its Memorandum Circular (MC) No. 24, s. 20073 expressly excluded local government units from its coverage. As to the last issue, similarly, the Department had on one occasion an opportunity to discuss whether a person may have access to information relative to a barangay's payroll. In the DILG Opinion No. 63 s. 2019, we opined that a barangay payroll is regarded as an official record/document in the custody of a government agency/oficial which must be accessible to the public. However, in the case of Atty. Mark, and by virtue of his engagement under a contract of service, he is not regarded a govemment employee; hence, his payroll is not deemed a public document and is not instantly accessible to the public. We opine that a Special Power of Attorney (SPA) from Atty. Mark is necessary if you want to obtain access to this information. Finally, this Department's opinion is based solely on the facts and representations narrated from the letter and our appreciation of the same. Further, this opinion is being 2 Civil Service Commission vs. Pililla Water District, G.R. No. 190147, March 5, 2013. 3 GUIDELINES IN THE DECLARATION OF POSITIONS IN GOVERNMENT AGENCIES (EXCLUDING LGUS) AS PRIMARILY CONFIDENTIAL, Deæmber 13, 2007. Page 2 of 3

rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you on this matter. Thank you very much. Very truly yours, BY AUT ORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ÅTTY. UA VI OR R. LLAMAS Undersecr ry for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUS Page 3 of 3
